source: The single source for every "what if I did X" in the app: one line a lever, the size of each move stated as a plain assumption. A side hustle netting $500 a month, a house hack cutting the rent line by 40%, a move somewhere a quarter cheaper, a job change worth 20% more, a 3% real raise kept or spent. Illustrative starting points chosen to be arguable, not measured averages; every room that offers a lever prints its figure beside the number it moves and lets it be changed.
confidenceNote: Teaching devices. No study says a house hack cuts housing by 40% for you; it says it can. The figures are the defaults a room starts from, never findings.
note: Read by shared/levers.js and, for the five opening levers (payStep, spendCut, returnUp, clearDearest, halfRaise; D-312), by engines/opening.js, which applies their moves in its own three-number model: income.takeHomeMonthlyCents is absolute cents of take-home, expenses.* a share of spending, assumptions.returnReal an absolute change to the real return, debt.dearest clears the highest-rate debt and frees its payment, income.raiseKeptShare is the share of each raise saved at the opening file's real raise rate. shared/levers.js leaves those keys alone. No room may inline a lever figure again (D-174). `moves` values: absolute cents when the key ends in `Cents`, otherwise a share of the current figure, positive or negative. `appliesWhen` is one of a few fixed phrases the library knows how to read; it is not evaluated as code. Implied hourly wage = monthly gain ÷ (hoursPerWeek × 4.33), computed in the library.

payStep.label: Earn $500 more a month, after tax
payStep.flex: a raise, a switch or a second job

returnUp.label: Earn one point more on what is invested
